summary: Abraham Hyacinthe Anquetil-Duperron worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied theology at the Sorbonne and at Amersfoort, and under Dasturs Darab and Kaus. He held posts at the Bibliothèque nationale and Institut de France.

Abraham Richard Fuller was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. A Major in the Royal Artillery and Lieutenant in the Bengal Army (1849), he served as Director of the Department of Public Instruction, Punjab, from 1860 to 1867.

Abraham Sachs was a scholar of history, archaeology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Johns Hopkins University (c. 1933–1937) and held posts at the Institute for Advanced Study (1945) and Brown University (c. 1945–1983).

Abraham Yohannan worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University under A. V. Williams Jackson from around 1895 to 1898 and held a post at Columbia from around 1894 to 1925.
Abraham Zablocki specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from Cornell University and held a post at Agnes Scott College (attested 2008).
Acharya Buddharakkhita studied under Anton Walter Florus Gueth (c. 1952–1956), Mahasi Sayadaw (c. 1953–1956), and U Nārada, and later taught Laurence Khantipalo Mills.

Achim Bayer specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his MA and PhD at the University of Hamburg under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen, holding posts at the University of Munich (2004–2006) and Hamburg (attested 2026).

Achyutananda Dash specializes in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He was a Commonwealth Visiting Fellow at the University of Oxford (1997–1998) and held a post at Dr. Hari Singh Gour University (attested 1999).

Ada Maryla Falk worked in Indology and religious studies. She studied at the University of Florence under Paolo Emilio Pavolini and Sapienza University of Rome under Pettazzoni, Formichi, and Tucci, later teaching at Sapienza (c. 1937–1963) and Calcutta (1939).

Adalbert Bezzenberger worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Göttingen under Theodor Benfey and Munich under Martin Haug, later holding posts at Göttingen (1874) and as Professor of Sanskrit and IE at the University of Königsberg (1879–1921).

Adalbert J. Gail worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He completed his doctoral studies under Helmut Hoffmann (c. 1964–1968) and served as a professor at the Free University of Berlin from around 1978 to 2006.

Adalbert Kuhn was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his PhD at Humboldt University of Berlin under Franz Bopp and served in teaching and directorship roles at Cöllnisches Gymnasium between 1837 and 1870.

Adam Bowles specializes in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at La Trobe University under Greg Bailey and became Associate Professor in Asian Religions at the University of Queensland in 2009.

Adam Hardy specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied architecture at Trinity College, Cambridge, and held professorships at De Montfort University (c. 1993–2003) and Cardiff University (from 2004).

Adam Heinz was a linguist who studied at the University of Lviv under Jerzy Kuryłowicz and earned his PhD at Jagiellonian University under Jan Safarewicz. He held posts at the Pedagogical University of Krakow and Jagiellonian University (1957–1984).
Adam Hohenberger was a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Ernst Windisch (c. 1908–1912) and earned his PhD from the University of Leipzig (1913–1918).

Adam Miller specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago and has held teaching posts at Heartland Community College, Western Illinois University, Towson University, and Mercyhurst University.

Adam Pearcey is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at SOAS University of London under Ulrich Pagel, Nathan W. Hill, and Vincent Tournier, and serves as Senior Editor and Translator for Lotsawa House.

Adam Yuet Chau specializes in Sinology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Stanford University and holds posts at the University of Cambridge as Professor of the Anthropology of China (from 2008) and Fellow at St John's College.
Adele Schlombs works in Sinology, history, and archaeology. She held posts at the Museum of East-Asian Art (1991) and the Museum für Ostasiatische Kunst Köln (c. 1991–2022).
